name: Faustine Yamamoto
title: Analytics projects with their limits stated
description: Five data analytics case studies on hospital readmissions, coupon acceptance, product launches, the gender earnings gap and airline delays.
intro: MSc Business Analytics student at the University of Greenwich (Product Development pathway), based in London. These are five pieces of coursework written up as short case studies: what was asked, what the data showed, and what it cannot show.

projects.question: Can data available at discharge predict which patients come back?
projects.result: A class-weighted SVC caught 68 of 79 readmitted patients
projects.methods: Logistic regression, support vector classifier, class weighting, K-means and hierarchical clustering

projects.question: What makes a driver accept a coupon?
projects.result: Cheap-meal coupons are accepted about 7 in 10 times, bar coupons about 4 in 10
projects.data: 12,007 driving scenarios from the UCI in-vehicle coupon dataset
projects.methods: Random forest, decision tree, logistic regression, Apriori association rules

projects.question: Which levers raise the chance a product launch succeeds?
projects.result: Four levers explain 59% of the variation in launch success
projects.methods: Simple and multiple linear regression with assumption diagnostics

projects.question: How large is the gender pay gap, and do age and education explain it?
projects.result: About 15% lower hourly pay for women, stable across ten specifications
projects.data: 149,316 workers from a 2014 US labour-force survey extract
projects.methods: Log-wage regression with age and education controls

projects.question: What drives airline delays, and when do they peak?
projects.result: Late-arriving aircraft cause 40% of delay minutes
